result.title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
result.comment: Accepted as a Spotlight paper at NeurIPS 2026. Our code is available at https://github.com/THUMAI-Lab/RiT
result.summary: Latent Diffusion Models dominate generative modeling but face two-stage training complexity and the inherent reconstruction limits of pre-trained autoencoders. Pixel-space Flow Matching offers a simplified end-to-end alternative yet often encounters training difficulties when using the standard $v$-prediction objective. Recent research attributes this difficulty to the off-manifold nature of noised targets, motivating a shift toward $x$-prediction. In this paper, we investigate this explanation through patch-wise Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and identify a bandwidth bottleneck. The velocity in minor components is largely determined by the raw noisy input, requiring deep backbones to preserve information that competes with principal-component modeling. Through controlled experiments and representation analysis, we further examine why $x$-prediction remains effective: its parameterization provides a raw-input bypass, while its learned input representation can spontaneously concentrate on principal directions. Under low-rank observations, our analysis of the induced flow characterizes $x$-prediction as an implicit conditional-mean decoder, reconstructing discarded components from the retained information. These observations motivate the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT), which combines a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder with an output-side shortcut to separate semantic modeling from raw-state propagation. Our method restores effective $v$-prediction and achieves competitive performance on ImageNet $256\times256$, providing a perspective on the interaction between prediction objectives and architectural bandwidth.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以 patch-wise PCA 分析像素空间 flow matching 中 v-prediction 的训练困难，指出次要主成分方向上的带宽瓶颈，并解释 x-prediction 有效性的来源是原始输入旁路和表示向主方向自发集中；据此提出分离语义建模与原始状态传递的 Raw-injected Transformer（RiT）。
